literal: Gain aiming at, capital losing action, will not undertake those who possess wisdom.
translation: Those who possess wisdom will not undertake an action that risks losing their existing capital in the pursuit of profit.
modern: இலாபத்தை எதிர்பார்த்து, முதலீட்டையே இழக்கச் செய்யும் செயலை அறிவுடையவர்கள் செய்யத் தொடங்க மாட்டார்கள்.
explanation: This couplet advises on the importance of risk assessment before starting any venture. The word 'ākkam' refers to the expected profit or growth, while 'mutal' refers to the base capital or existing assets. Wise people ('aṟivuṭaiyār') will not be motivated ('ūkkār') to initiate an action ('ceyviṉai') if a careful analysis reveals that the pursuit of extra gain might end up destroying the very foundation of what they already own. Preserving one's core resources is prioritized over speculative and highly risky gains.
